lines.text: A new product launches next quarter.
How long until it shows up in your forecast?
In most teams, a new revenue stream means a new tab, a new file and a week of rework.
And nobody can say how it splits by project or by department.
In NetSuite Planning, revenue lives in one model.
Add a stream once, and every view of your forecast picks it up.
Forecast by amount, or by units and price.
Compare scenarios and versions, and report on any dimension.
Here is how it works.
From the home page, open Revenue and Gross Margin.
Then set your point of view: the forecast scenario, the working version and the currency.
The Revenue Input Sheet has rows by project, department and class, and columns by forecast year.
To add a new stream, pick the class for it, and the project and department it belongs to.
Enter the amounts by year, and save.
Need it by month?
Enter the annual amount, and Planning spreads it across the months using your seasonality.
Or type each month directly.
For product lines, forecast units and price instead.
Planning multiplies them, and revenue is calculated for you.
On save, Planning runs the rules for you.
Currency is converted, and the stream rolls up to total revenue, in seconds.
Now look at the same number by project.
Every project shows its share of revenue, year by year.
Switch the view to department.
Same total, now split by the teams that own it.
And by category: product, services, and the new stream you just added.
One model, three views, and they always tie out.
Then compare the forecast against the budget, side by side.
You see exactly where the new stream moves the number.
From there, revenue flows into the P and L and the forecast reports.
No copy and paste, no second version of the truth.
Write to Bryant Park Consulting to forecast revenue in NetSuite Planning.
And get the most out of your implementation.
